subject: potential memory issues at addSNPs step?

messages.author: 43bf2fdc8e90d845
messages.subject: potential memory issues at addSNPs step?
parts:
Hello!

I am running into a problem with the addSNPs function - working with 10 gwas summary statistics and completed the ldsc step (#2) and the sumstats step (#3) [same file order, as indicated on the wiki]. When I start the addSNPs command, I run out of memory before it completes - and I'm working on a cluster with 1TB of ram, so I assume I'm doing something wrong! So, a couple questions:

1. is the ldsc input file the entire output from the ldsc step, or is it just the S and V matrix?
2. is it possible to pipe out some of the S and V matrices that are created for every SNP to some results folder, or do all of the matrices need to be held in memory simultaneously?
3. When I submit the addSNPs command (printed below), I see this output in my window:
[1] 1
[1] 10000
[1] 20000
[1] 30000
[1] 40000
...
But in addSNPs.R, it looks like maybe I should be seeing "Creating Sampling Covariance [V] matrices"?

Any and all ideas would be helpful. Thank you! And thank you for the package :o)

load("LDSC_allsumstats_111919.RData")
load("sumstats_all.RData")
SNPcov_all<-addSNPs(LDSC_allsumstats_111919,sumstats_all,SNPSE=FALSE,parallel=FALSE,cores=NULL)

Thank you
Arianna

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: potential memory issues at addSNPs step?
parts:
Hi Arianna, 

Thanks for posting! For your first question, the ldsc file is the entire output from the matrix. For your second question, since each run of Genomic SEM in multivariate GWAS is independent of one another, you can split the sumstats file into smaller chunks of 40k SNPs and then run addSNPs and save the output, or directly put it into a multivariate GWAS function and save that output. 

It is surprising that you are running out of memory on a 1TB machine at only 40k SNPs. I would suggest trying to set parallel to TRUE and see if you run into the same problem? I'll note that you would only see "Creating Sampling Covariance [V] matrices" as a message if you run addSNPs in parallel, whereas it will show a running count for every 10k SNPs (like you posted) if you run in serial. I know other groups (including our own) have created scripts that will automatically chunk the sumstats file and send it off to different jobs to avoid things like memory issues and to speed things up, but we aren't at the point of being ready to share those yet because some of the commands are still specific to our computing cluster and will cause all sorts of errors when used generally. More importantly though, I'm just about done with a new function that combines addSNPs and the GWAS functions into one function, where it creates the matrices one at a time and discards them when done with the single run, which should help with memory issues. I expect to have that up on the github within the next few days and will post here when it's ready, so depending on your timeline you can also sit tight for that. Let me know if any other questions pop up in the mean time!

-Andrew
